subject: SKU-level commit: surcharge scenarios, approval path, and next steps
messages:
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>, Sara Liu <sara.liu@brightleaf.ai>
Cc: BrightLeaf Legal <legal@brightleaf.ai>
Date: Tue, 28 Oct 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: SKU-level commit: surcharge scenarios, approval path, and next steps

Sara / team — thanks again for the conversation yesterday. I pulled together the sku-level commit sensitivity worksheet (attached) that maps BrightLeaf's projected usage to Redwood's reserved capacity SKU mix and the incremental surcharge that would apply under three GPU-cost scenarios. High level:

- Scenario A (stable GPU spot prices): minimal surcharge, discounts as proposed in the term sheet.
- Scenario B (+15% GPU price pressure): moderate surcharge on high-memory SKUs unless BrightLeaf shifts some load to lower-memory variants.
- Scenario C (+30% GPU price shock): surcharge + requirement for cross-region fallback capacity for critical SLAs.

Attachments: reserved_commit_model_mix.xlsx (spreadsheet) and nvidia_quote_Q3.pdf (vendor quote supporting cost deltas).

Action items I want to align on:
1) Confirm which SKUs BrightLeaf is comfortable committing to (percent of total).
2) Agree approval path internally at Redwood for >15% surcharge triggers.
3) If needed, request an expedited NVIDIA approval for a temporary unit discount tied to the deal.

Marissa / Evelyn — I sketched an approval path in the draft doc (attached). If we can get internal OK for a one-time approval threshold (e.g., up to 12% surcharge without exec sign-off), we can close quicker.

Sara — can you confirm the expected monthly token throughput per SKU (or upload point estimates to the attached sheet)? That will let us finalize the pricing table.

Thanks,
Ben

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>

Date: Tue, 28 Oct 2026 11:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: SKU-level commit: surcharge scenarios, approval path, and next steps

Ben — good work on the sensitivity matrix. A couple of notes from Pricing/Finance:

- We need SKU breakout across GPU families (A100/RTX/NextGen) not just memory tiers. The cost sensitivity differs by family; please ask BrightLeaf to tag preferred models in the sheet.
- Finance will pre-approve up to 10% surcharge across the life of the commit provided BrightLeaf moves 20% of their inference workload to lower-memory variants during Q1. Anything >10% requires VP approval (Rishi).

Evelyn — can you draft the one-page exec memo we can use to request VP approval if we cross 10%? Include the estimated revenue upside and delegation of authority.

Sara — noted on the request for monthly throughput; thanks for filling that in.

Marissa
Marissa Cole
Head of Pricing & Commercial Operations

From: Sara Liu <sara.liu@brightleaf.ai>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Cc: BrightLeaf Legal <legal@brightleaf.ai>
Date: Wed, 29 Oct 2026 08:17:00 -0700
Subject: Re: SKU-level commit: surcharge scenarios, approval path, and next steps

Ben / Marissa — thanks for the breakdown. A few clarifying Qs from procurement and legal before we sign:

1) How will the surcharge be calculated and invoiced? We need a clear formula in the contract (example: surcharge = max(0, (observed vendor GPU cost index - baseline) * surcharge_rate)).
2) Is there a cap on total surcharge over the term? Our CFO pushed back on open-ended pass-throughs.
3) Can Redwood commit to a 30-day notice before any surcharge goes live so we can review mitigation options?

We are OK with the idea of moving some load to lower-memory SKUs but need Redwood to model the expected quality delta (latency / accuracy) in the attached sheet.

Sara Liu
Sr. Procurement Manager, BrightLeaf AI
sara.liu@brightleaf.ai
From: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
Cc: Sara Liu <sara.liu@brightleaf.ai>
Date: Fri, 31 Oct 2026 14:30:00 -0700
Subject: Re: SKU-level commit: surcharge scenarios, approval path, and next steps

All — draft answers below that I will fold into a short approval memo and the amendment language for legal.

- Surcharge formula: agree with Sara's suggested approach. We'll anchor to a vendor GPU-cost index (NVIDIA list + freight/driver license delta) and apply a surcharge rate per SKU. We'll include worked examples in the amendment.
- Cap: propose a cap at 18% of the annual reserved spend (not per-invoice). That gives us protection while addressing BrightLeaf's concern about open-ended pass-throughs.
- Notice: 30-day notice accepted. We'll also add a 60-day bilateral review clause for major (>20%) shifts.

Approval path (recommended):
- Up to 10% surcharge: pricing team sign-off (Marissa).
- 10%–18%: VP approval (Rishi).
- >18%: Executive committee review + sales ops and CFO sign-off.

If we need a temporary NVIDIA unit discount (to keep BrightLeaf at commit), I'll open a channel with NVIDIA Sales — Sara, I'm including them on thread (see attached vendor quote previously). Ben, please confirm whether we want me to request a one-time adjustment and provide the negotiation target (bps off list).

Eve
Evelyn Hart
Director, Customer Success & Contracts

Subject: Re: SKU-level commit: surcharge scenarios, approval path, and next steps

Quick update / next steps we agreed on in internal call this morning:

1) BrightLeaf to confirm SKU preferences and fill throughput numbers in reserved_commit_model_mix.xlsx by EOD Thursday (5 Nov).
2) Redwood will insert the surcharge formula and example table into the amendment; cap will be 18% of annual reserved spend.
3) Approval path confirmed as Evelyn proposed (<=10% Marissa; 10–18% Rishi; >18% exec).
4) Evelyn to open outreach to NVIDIA for a one-time unit discount target of 7% off list if we hit Scenario B likelihood (>15%). Evelyn will loop NVIDIA Sales (cc'd).
5) Legal to draft amendment language with 30-day notice and bilateral 60-day review clause. BrightLeaf Legal to comment.

Sara — thanks for the transparency on the cap/notice ask. Once we have your filled sheet I'll produce the amendment redline and a one-page exec memo for Rishi. I'll also include the DocuSign link for signature-ready documents (placeholder below).

DocuSign (placeholder): https://docusign.com/brightleaf/ds12345
